title: sa-engine record container (.saenet transport traces, .saerec session records)

types.note: bytes[n] is n raw bytes; fourcc is 4 ASCII bytes. All integers are little-endian. Every offset is relative to the start of the structure it names.

fields.name: index_offset
fields.note: 0 = the file was not finalized (no chunk table)

fields.name: dt_s_us
fields.note: server tick period in microseconds, 0 = unknown

FINALIZED.meaning: the chunk table is present and index_offset, chunk_count and the time range are valid

COMPRESSED.meaning: at least one chunk has codec other than 0

SORTED.meaning: chunk time ranges are in non-decreasing order

MERGED.meaning: records of several nodes; every record carries 'node'

flags.reserved: bits 4..31 are written as 0; a reader ignores unknown bits of the same major version

2.name: zstd
2.meaning: reserved; a version 1 reader may report UNSUPPORTED

fields.name: stored_size
fields.note: payload bytes as stored (after compression), without padding

fields.name: raw_size
fields.note: payload bytes after decompression (= stored_size for codec 0)

fields.name: rec_count
fields.note: records in the payload; 0 for chunks that hold no records

fields.name: crc32
fields.note: crc32 of the stored payload bytes

chunk_header.layout: chunk header (40 bytes), payload (stored_size bytes), zero padding up to the next multiple of 8 bytes from the start of the chunk

META.payload: one UTF-8 JSON object: the 'hdr' record of the sae-obs/1 stream

OBSJ.payload: UTF-8 JSON Lines: sae-obs/1 records (not hdr), one per line, '\n' terminated

BLOB.payload: u16 name length, UTF-8 name, then opaque bytes

SAEX.payload: the chunk table (see 'table'); never listed in the table itself

table.layout: magic fourcc, entry_count u32, entry_size u32 (48), reserved u32 (0), then entry_count entries, then table_crc32 u32 over everything from the magic to the last entry, then end_magic fourcc 'XEAS'

fields.name: offset
fields.note: file offset of the chunk header

fields.name: chunk_header
fields.note: a copy of the chunk header

limits.note: A reader refuses chunks whose raw_size exceeds its limit (default 256 MiB) and never decompresses beyond raw_size.
